properties.state: {"concern":"core","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"The design says which interfaces are the published boundaries, and computations read that distinction","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Some interfaces are the boundary a system is known by; most are internal plumbing. The design must be able to say which — and the distinction must earn its keep by being read, not merely stored (dec:edge-orthogonality). From the MOSA guidebook Anthony supplied (OUSD(R&E), February 2025), whose entire discipline turns on designating modular system interfaces and then holding them stable and open, and independently from BL-45's system-of-systems thread, which found the same hole from the other side: nothing marks an Interface external-facing, so \"visible to others\" versus \"mine to change\" is undeclarable. Two independent routes to one missing property. What must read it, or the designation is decoration: a change that crosses a published boundary is a different risk from one that stays behind it, and impact analysis should say which it is BEFORE the edit; a design that publishes a surface should be able to export exactly that surface and nothing internal; and a composed design (req:design-composes) links through published boundaries, never through another system's internals. What this must NOT become: an assertion that a boundary is stable. Whether a published interface has in fact held is a matter of evidence — its drift history — not a property anyone sets.","status":"accepted"}
